title: decision-ledger-rollout-advisor-and-cost-aware-shadow-seeder
author: Lina Morales
body: Motivation: We need a deterministic, auditable record of rollout decisions (promote, hold, rollback) that can be replayed and simulated to answer operator questions and automate rollback suggestions. This PR introduces a lightweight decision ledger and an advisory layer that synthesizes telemetry, cost signals, and counterfactual replay to provide safe canary/A-B/shadow promos. Design summary: 1) decision_ledger service stores immutable decision events (reason, inputs, heuristics, confidence) and exposes a read/write API for the rollout controller; 2) rollout_advisor component ingests live telemetry streams plus recent ledger entries and computes an action recommendation (promote/retain/backout/partial-backout) with an explainability payload; 3) shadow_seeder implements a cost-aware reservoir sampler that seeds shadow traffic across slices based on unit-cost budgets and quality risk; 4) a counterfactual replayer re-executes a bounded sample of requests against candidate model revisions using stored KV prefixes and deterministic RNG to estimate delta metrics; 5) safety gates include sample-size thresholds, latency/cost SLO thresholds, and a multi-metric risk score that weights user-impacting regressions higher than cost regressions. Implementation notes: The decision ledger is implemented as an append-only protobuf log with local write buffering and durable flush to the existing rollout-snapstore. The advisor exposes a gRPC endpoint used by the rollout controller; recommendations are annotated with evidence keys that map to ledger entries and telemetry traces for audit. The shadow seeder introduces a small policy DSL (JSON) to express cost caps per cohort and decay windows. The counterfactual replayer runs off a dedicated worker pool and emits a synthesized delta metric event that the advisor consumes. Testing: Added unit tests for ledger ordering and idempotency, property tests for the reservoir sampler, an e2e flow test that runs a simulated canary (10k synthetic requests) and validates advisor decisions under injected latency regressions, and a small chaos test that verifies safe backout when the ledger becomes temporarily unreachable. CI story: initial CI run failed integration tests due to a race in the snapshot flush path under high concurrency (flaky: tests/rollout/test_snapshot_race.py). The fix introduces a per-snapshot write lock and reduces flush window drift; all tests and linters pass after the fix. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior is no-op unless the operator enables the decision-ledger flag. Rolling rollout of this PR will be gated with a feature flag at the controller level and an admin UI toggle in the Console. Security and privacy: ledger entries can be redacted by policy; no raw user inputs are written. Observability: added new metrics rollout_decisions_total, rollout_advisor_latency_seconds_bucket, counterfactual_delta_histogram, and a debug trace tag advisor.evidence_id that links to trace and ledger event. Docs: updated docs/rollouts/decision-ledger.md and added a short runbook in docs/rollouts/runbooks/rollback-advisor.md. Related work: builds on past canary frameworks (see ENG-1022) and complements the automated rollback advisor in SUP-9123. Migration notes: existing rollout snapshots remain compatible; a migration script (tools/ledger/migrate_snapshots.py) converts legacy snapshot metadata to ledger pointers. Why this is different: rather than only reacting to threshold breaches, the advisor reasons over a small universe of counterfactual outcomes and cost constraints and then records each decision for later forensic replay. This enables reproducible incident analysis and cautious automation.
commits: Initialize decision ledger core and proto definitions
Implement advisor gRPC shim and basic risk scorer
Add shadow seeder reservoir policy DSL
Wire counterfactual replayer worker and metrics emission
Fix snapshot flush race by adding write lock and tests
Add e2e rollout flow test and runbook docs
review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice isolation of ledger I/O, please add a short note about retention policy and compaction on the proto file so operators aren't surprised.
Lina Morales: Added compaction/retention section to decision_ledger.proto and docs; ledger uses configurable retention window and compact-to-references beyond 90d.
Marcus López: The advisor risk weights look reasonable but we should expose them as a tunable policy; can we default to conservative values?
Lina Morales: Exposed risk weights in advisor config with conservative defaults (safety bias = 1.5, cost_bias = 0.5).
Priya Patel: The e2e seemed slow in CI; can we make synthetic traffic deterministic so reproducing fails is easier?
Lina Morales: Made the synthetic request generator deterministic via seed and reduced sample size for CI; full-scale sim runs in nightly tests.
Ava Chen: Approving after the snapshot lock fix and docs updates.
Marcus López: Minor nit in seeder policy parsing fixed in last commit.
CI Bot: Integration tests failed on first run (snapshot race). Rerun requested and passed.
release_notes: Added decision ledger and rollout advisor: opt-in feature flag, cost-aware shadow seeding, counterfactual replayer, new telemetry metrics, and runbook. Operators should review retention default and advisor config before enabling in production.
